newsitem.title: RUSSIA: India says Russian nuclear station project cleared.
newsitem.headline: India says Russian nuclear station project cleared.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Tuesday he has sorted out problems which have stalled a 1988 contract under which Russia undertook to build a nuclear power station in the southern state of Tamil Nadu.

"Some of the issues have been pending since 1988 including two nuclear power stations," Deve Gowda told reporters after talks with Chernomyrdin in a reference to two reactors due to be supplied for the Kudankulam nuclear power station.
"Today the agreement about two nuclear power stations was finalised," he added without giving any details.
The main stumbling block had been that India wanted to pay mostly in consumer goods while Moscow was keen to get cash.
"I don't know what they finally decided," Russian ministry spokesman Georgy Kaurov said. "But if the minister says something was agreed that means the problem was sorted out."

Kaurov had said earlier that as soon as financial problems were solved construction could start and be completed in several years. He said the next stage would be working out a precise construction scheme and deciding which Russian firms take part.
